reception: External reception likewise comes from builders. The dynamic binary translation community treats the paper as a reference on code-cache consistency and capacity: the DynamoRIO line extended it to thread-shared and process-shared, persistent code caches, while independent systems engage it on its own ground — fragment-cache management for embedded scratchpads and work on reducing pressure in bounded DBT code caches position their schemes against it, and HDTrans, generators of low-overhead binary translators, and process-level redundancy work on transient fault tolerance cite its measurements as evidence. The remaining citations are brief mentions in the same literature; almost nothing cites the paper from outside the community that manages code caches. The DynamoRIO system lives on in the DynamoRIO/dynamorio repository.
